output.brief:
The failures are caused by rate limiting at the payment gateway, not by release v4.12. On 3 March at 09:00, before v4.12 deployed, Finance's settle-recon job began running every 15 minutes on the same gateway credential checkout uses. Each run sends 360–430 search calls per minute, over the 300/min limit, so Quillmark returns HTTP 429 and checkout payments in those minutes fail. v4.12 hid the real status by mapping every error to "declined". Evidence: 93% of failures fall in the first minutes of each quarter hour; no clusters occurred during the finance maintenance window; and rolling half the pods back to v4.11 gave the same failure rate (3.7% vs 3.6%), with 341 of 351 failures being 429s. Issuer declines are flat.
Next: pause settle-recon's daytime runs or revert it to nightly now, and watch the 429 and failure rates. Give it its own credential before any daytime schedule. Don't roll back v4.12; the rollback would lose the card-masking fix due by 13 March. Don't attribute the 9% revenue fall to the failures. Conversion, order value and the promotion changed too, so estimate the failure effect separately once fixed. A rate-limit increase is slow and chargeable, and wouldn't fix the cause. Confidence is high, and a recovery after the pause would confirm it.
